scope: Requested-field proposal only; never an answer, fact, authorization, entity resolution or player progress decision.

labels.identity: Definition, identity or occupational role of a subject.
labels.purpose: Intended function, reason for existence, or a person's own motivation.
labels.relationship: Connection, kinship or affiliation between subjects.
labels.installation: Installing, building, compiling or initially setting up software.
labels.configuration: Selecting or inspecting settings, parameters, registry values or operating modes.
labels.download: A source, repository or URL for obtaining digital software, binaries or source code.
labels.documentation: A manual, API reference, instructions document or documentation URL.
labels.support: A human/community help channel or place to report issues.
labels.compatibility: Whether two editions, platforms or components can operate together.
labels.version: A release number, architecture, toolchain or runtime version.
labels.location: Where a subject currently exists or can be found.
labels.destination: Where a movement, transfer, exit or placement ends.
labels.route: A path or travel directions to a place.
labels.acquisition: Obtaining a physical or in-world item, reward or resource.
labels.recruitment: Convincing or hiring a person to join or accompany a party.
labels.prerequisites: Conditions, permissions, materials or quantities required before an action.
labels.stats: Numeric attributes, costs, durations, formulas or quantitative properties, excluding required resources.
labels.combat: Fighting tactics, combat capabilities, weaknesses or attack selection.
labels.use: When/how to operate an item or ability, including its inherent effect.
labels.method: A non-specialized procedure, action, menu, keyword or way to accomplish a task.
labels.outcome: An event's result, reward, consequence or state change after a choice/action.
labels.cause: An explanatory cause of an observed event or condition.
labels.creator: Who authored, made, wrote or developed a subject.
labels.comparison: A contrast, relative merit or recommendation between alternatives.
labels.limitations: Restrictions, caveats, risks, unsupported features or finite capacity.
labels.objective: The player's/task operator's goal or next task to achieve.
labels.sequence: The ordering of tasks or events, what precedes/follows what.
labels.remedy: Corrective action for a stated failure, error or undesired condition.
labels.reference: A general statement/property verification or source reference when no specific field applies.

hierarchy: Split independent questions before this classifier; each sample requests one primary field.
Classify the requested field, retaining negation, numbers, sources and editions in the untouched input; those qualifiers do not establish truth or support.
URLs are classified by requested resource: documentation before generic source/download, community help as support, obtaining binaries/source code as download.
Failure plus requested fix is remedy; why the failure occurred is cause; settings sought as values are configuration; first installation/build steps are installation.
Location is the present/found position; destination is the endpoint or placement target; route is how to travel there.
Digital assets use download; in-world items use acquisition; people joining use recruitment.
An item's intended function is purpose; operation or inherent effect of that item is use; a general task procedure is method; an event/choice consequence is outcome.
Objective is what goal the operator must achieve; purpose includes another actor's motivation; sequence explicitly asks order.
Required resources/permissions are prerequisites even if numeric; a descriptive cost/statistic is stats; explicit fighting strategy/capability is combat.
Compatibility is interoperability; comparison asks differences or relative merits; limitations asks a restriction; version asks release/toolchain identity.
Reference is the residual verification/source request only after specific field meanings; unknown is omitted because abstention is a separate thresholded action.
